lesson.title: Git Rebase and Conflict Resolution
lesson.goal: rebase a feature branch onto main with git and resolve the conflicts

steps.title: Set up repo and check branches
steps.instructions: From an empty folder, run the setup command to create a repo whose main and feature/login branches both change index.js and package.json, so they will conflict. Then run git branch -a and git status to confirm you are on feature/login with a clean tree.

targets.caption: Confirm you are on the unpushed feature branch before rebasing

explanations.topic: How git rebase replays commits onto a new base commit
Checking remote branches with git branch -a
How to abort a rebase with git rebase --abort
Why rebase resolves conflicts one commit at a time

hints: Make sure you run the setup commands inside an empty directory.
Use git branch -a to verify that no remotes/origin branch exists for your feature branch.
Run git checkout feature/login and git status so the working tree is clean on your feature branch.
common_mistakes: Rebasing a branch that has already been pushed and pulled by teammates.
Running the rebase while still checked out on main instead of the feature branch.
steps.code: git init -b main && echo '{"name":"git-rebase-example","version":"1.0.0","main":"index.js","scripts":{"start":"node index.js"},"dependencies":{"express":"^4.17.1"}}' > package.json && echo 'const express = require("express"); const app = express(); const port = 3000; const DEFAULT_USER = "guest"; app.use(express.json()); app.get("/", (req, res) => res.send("Welcome")); app.listen(port);' > index.js && git add . && git commit -m "Initial commit" && git checkout -b feature/login && sed -i.bak 's/"guest"/"admin"/' index.js && rm -f index.js.bak && git commit -am "Add login endpoint" && git commit --allow-empty -m "Add logout endpoint" && sed -i.bak 's/"start":"node index.js"/"start":"node index.js","check":"node --check index.js"/' package.json && rm -f package.json.bak && git commit -am "Add authentication middleware" && git checkout main && sed -i.bak 's/"guest"/"john"/' index.js && rm -f index.js.bak && sed -i.bak 's/"start":"node index.js"/"start":"node index.js","check":"node -c index.js"/' package.json && rm -f package.json.bak && git commit -am "Add user profile and logging" && git checkout feature/login

steps.title: Rebase feature branch onto main
steps.instructions: From feature/login, run git rebase main to replay your commits on top of main. When Git stops at the first conflict, run git status to see the rebase progress.

targets.caption: Git pauses the rebase at the first conflicting commit

hints: Which branch name do you pass to git rebase when you want main as the new base?
Run git rebase main while checked out on feature/login.
Run git status after the conflict message to see which file is marked as both modified.
common_mistakes: Running git rebase feature/login while on feature/login instead of git rebase main.
Panicking at the conflict error and trying to start a new rebase instead of inspecting git status.

steps.title: Resolve first conflict in index.js
steps.instructions: Open index.js, delete the conflict markers, and keep the DEFAULT_USER value you want (the tutorial keeps "admin"). Save, run git add index.js, then git status.

targets.caption: Remove the conflict markers and choose the final value for DEFAULT_USER
Git confirms the conflict is resolved

hints: Look for the <<<<<<< HEAD, =======, and >>>>>>> markers inside index.js.
Delete the marker lines and the incoming/current duplicate lines you do not want, keeping const DEFAULT_USER = "admin";.
Save index.js and run git add index.js followed by git status.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to delete one of the <<<<<<<, =======, or >>>>>>> marker lines before staging.
Running git commit instead of staging with git add during a rebase.

steps.title: Continue rebase and save commit message
steps.instructions: Run git rebase --continue to apply the resolved commit and move on to the remaining commits. When Vim opens the commit message, press Escape, type :wq, and press Enter, then continue until the next conflict or the end of the rebase.

precision_checks.label: No unmerged files remain
precision_checks.command: test -z "$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U)" || git status | grep -q 'rebase in progress'

targets.caption: Git committed your resolved change and continued the rebase
Rebase paused at the next conflicting commit

explanations.topic: Exiting Vim with :wq when editing commit messages
Resolving the final commit conflict and verifying clean status

hints: Instead of git commit, which rebase subcommand resumes applying commits?
In Vim, press Esc, type :wq, and hit Enter to save the default commit message.
common_mistakes: Running git commit -m instead of git rebase --continue.
Getting stuck in Vim or quitting with :q! without saving when an editor opens.

steps.title: Resolve final conflict and finish rebase
steps.instructions: Open the conflicted file (package.json in the tutorial), remove the conflict markers keeping the version you want, and save it. Stage the file, run git rebase --continue (closing Vim with :wq), then run git status to confirm.

targets.caption: Keep the --check script and remove the conflict markers

hints: Edit package.json to keep only one valid "check" entry without any conflict markers.
Stage the file with git add package.json before continuing the rebase.
Run git rebase --continue, save and quit the commit message editor, then run git status.
common_mistakes: Leaving invalid JSON syntax (such as a trailing comma or duplicate key) in package.json after removing conflict markers.
Forgetting to run git rebase --continue after staging the last conflicted file.
steps.run_command: git add package.json && git rebase --continue && git status
